original.description: Studio portrait of John Charles Tashner Jr. in the dress blue uniform of a United States Navy chief petty officer: the chief's combination cap with the fouled-anchor-and-USN device, and aviation insignia above a ribbon bar. His service record lists Combat Aircrew Wings with Two Stars, and the family's research identifies the wings in this portrait as those. Undated; the chief's cap places it no earlier than his advancement to chief aviation radioman, which the record dates to 1944.
original.date: undated — 1944 or later, by the uniform against the service record
original.original_dimensions: 1087 × 1447 (colorized scan; the project does not yet hold the un-colorized original)
original.licence: private family photograph, Tashner family collection; supplied to this project by Jay Tashner's grandson in August 2026 with permission to publish, credited

colorization.author: Dave Tashner / Sandtable
colorization.method: AI-assisted colorization from the family's original print, 2026
colorization.licence: Sandtable project licence; underlying photograph Tashner family collection, used with permission
colorization.status: ok — label 'colorized (AI-assisted)'. CAUTION, and it is the family's own caution as well as ADR 0007's: ribbon colours in a colorization are not historical evidence. The documented award list in source:tashner-service-record is the authority — Combat Aircrew Wings with Two Stars, American Defense Medal with Fleet Clasp, Good Conduct Medal, Asiatic Pacific Ribbon with three stars, American Area Campaign Ribbon, World War II Victory Medal.

caption: John Charles Tashner Jr. — "Jay" (1920–1977), the Patrol Wing TWO radioman who is this pack's participant voice for 7 December 1941, photographed later in the war: the cap is a chief petty officer's, a rate his service record reaches in 1944, and the wings above the ribbons are his Combat Aircrew Wings. Colorized (AI-assisted) from a family photograph.
credit: Original photograph: Tashner family collection, undated; published with the family's permission. Colorization: Sandtable, AI-assisted, 2026.
notes: Supplied by the family (Dave Tashner, Jay's grandson) 2026-08-30. The identification of the sitter is the family's, consistent with the service record: the family's research dossier calls this 'the surviving uniform portrait' and matches its aviation insignia to the record's Combat Aircrew Wings (source:tashner-family-research-2026). The project holds only the colorized file; when the family digitizes the un-colorized print, add it as original.file so 'show original' can swap in place (ADR 0012). Not a period archive image — the one family-owned photograph the imagery policy has carried so far, admitted for the same reason the vignette was: a real participant, not a substitute for one.
